stem: A 34-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his partner due to agitation and confusion. He was recently started on a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) for major depressive disorder and has also been taking a prescription cough suppressant containing dextromethorphan over the last three days. Vitals are: temperature 39.4°C, pulse 118/min, blood pressure 152/94 mmHg, respiratory rate 22/min, and oxygen saturation 96% on room air. On physical examination, the patient is restless and agitated. Neurologic examination reveals hyperreflexia and rhythmic oscillations of the foot when the ankle is dorsiflexed. His pupils are 6 mm in diameter. There is no evidence of muscle rigidity.
lead_in: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: The patient presents with the classic triad of serotonin toxicity: mental status changes (agitation, confusion), autonomic instability (hyperthermia, tachycardia, hypertension, mydriasis), and neuromuscular excitability (hyperreflexia, ankle clonus). The combination of an SSRI and dextromethorphan (which has serotonergic properties) is a common trigger. Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) also presents with hyperthermia and altered mental status, but is characterized by 'lead-pipe' muscle rigidity and usually occurs after exposure to dopamine antagonists. Malignant hyperthermia presents with hyperthermia and rigidity, usually triggered by volatile anesthetics or succinylcholine. Anticholinergic toxicity presents with 'mad as a hatter' mental status and mydriasis, but lacks the hyperreflexia and clonus seen here. Sympathomimetic toxicity (e.g., cocaine, amphetamines) causes tachycardia and hypertension but does not typically feature the specific neuromuscular hyperreflexia and clonus pattern of serotonin toxicity.
teaching_point: Serotonin toxicity is characterized by a triad of mental status changes, autonomic instability, and neuromuscular excitability, specifically hyperreflexia and ankle clonus, often triggered by multiple serotonergic agents.

distractor_rationale.A: Presents with agitation and mydriasis, but lacks the hyperreflexia and clonus found in serotonin toxicity.
distractor_rationale.B: Triggered by certain anesthetics and characterized by severe muscle rigidity, not hyperreflexia/clonus.
distractor_rationale.C: Associated with dopamine antagonists and presents with 'lead-pipe' rigidity, not hyperreflexia.
distractor_rationale.E: Causes autonomic instability and agitation, but lacks the specific neuromuscular excitability of serotonin toxicity.
